subject: Vista Health renewal cadence, capacity uplift & QBR scheduling
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@vistahealth.io>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning - Vista Health (term + capacity)

Logan / Ben / Marcus,

Thanks for the run-through last week. As we approach our July 31 renewal I wanted to start a brief planning thread so we can align on the following: term length options, expected monthly token/embedding growth, and whether we should move from our current seat-based add-ons to a hybrid committed-usage model. High level asks from our side: 

- A refreshed proposal with a 12- versus 24-month term option and clear per-token economics at current usage + 30% and +60% forecasts.
- A short QBR (45 min) to review usage trends, capacity plan and run a mutual action plan for procurement/legal.
- A compliance touchpoint for our security folks to validate retention and audit log controls before signing.

I've attached a short capacity forecast (internal) to this email and flagged preferred QBR windows next week. Can you confirm who will own the contract contact and legal loop-in from your side?

Attachments: [attachment: capacity-forecast-2026.xlsx (Excel, 45KB)]

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Platform Integrations
Vista Health

1) Ben and Marcus will draft a 12- and 24-month proposal with blended per-token economics for the +30% and +60% scenarios.
2) I will schedule a 45-minute QBR during one of the windows you suggested; proposing three concrete slots below.
3) We'll include a brief compliance section in the proposal and ask Kimberly (legal & contracts) to join the procurement thread.

Proposed QBR slots (PDT):
- Tue 6/1 10:00–10:45
- Wed 6/2 14:00–14:45
- Thu 6/3 09:00–09:45

Can you confirm which slot works for Sam and your security contact? I'll circulate a calendar invite once confirmed.

Also attaching a lightweight proposal outline so Ben can fill pricing cells quickly.

Thanks — confirmed for Tue 6/1 10:00 PDT (calendar invite sent). Kimberly, Marissa — looping you both in for pricing guardrails and any legal playbook items. 

Ben / Marcus — action items for our prep: 
- Ben: populate the 12/24 month pricing table and include an optional committed-usage tier with defined uplifts at +30%/+60%. Attach draft PDF 'vista-renewal-proposal-v2.pdf' to the thread when ready.
- Marcus: prepare a short ops slide on prefix/KV caching and expected latency/cost delta at higher CTU (concurrency + throughput) so we can discuss capacity headroom.

Marissa — FYI this looks like a mid-size expansion (likely additional reserved capacity). If we surface a discount ask (customer will shop a 24-month term), what's the internal approver and typical approval band?

Kimberly — procurement will likely request a one-page SOW and minimal redlines. Can you confirm the turnaround for our standard renewal amendment?

I'll aim to circulate the draft proposal and a short pre-read by EOD Monday (6/7).

— Logan
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal planning - Vista Health (term + capacity)

Looping in approval path: for a deal this size (estimated ARR uplift in mid-six figures) discount approval flow is: AE -> Revenue Operations (Ben) -> Head of Sales (Marissa) -> CFO review if discount > 15%.

Kimberly: standard amendment turnaround is ~3 business days for non-material changes; if Vista requests contract language changes beyond liability caps or data residency we should expect longer.

Ben — please attach the populated proposal and a short ask summary (discount %, target ARR) so I can route quickly. I'll also join the QBR and handle executive alignment.
